# Text-fill luminance transforms

Original OPC/XML control generated by `tools/text_fill_luminance_fixture.py`
from the project's original outline/color fixtures. No corpus content, artwork
or font binaries are included; the control references installed Arial.

Twenty rows exercise literal and theme colors, ordered/repeated lumMod/lumOff,
zero, negative and greater-than-100% values, black/white, paragraph and character
style inheritance. The reference application opens the exact source and exports
the one-page `native.pdf` through `tools/export-reference.ps1`.
`tools/text_fill_luminance_reference.py` records each native PDF text fill color
and origin using PDFium and renders `native.png` at 96 DPI. Hashes bind the source,
case list, PDF and PNG. These expectations are not produced by the renderer.

The script also calculates independent Python colorsys HSL values. Row 12 is an
exact half-byte boundary: the reference application uses RGB 04/09/0D, while uncorrected floating-point
HSL arithmetic produces 8.499999999999998 for green and rounds down. Import keeps
intermediate channels unquantized and absorbs machine-epsilon error at the final
byte rounding. All twenty model colors match native PDF colors exactly.

The browser comparison tests both directions of the native/app glyph coverage
within one pixel, with less than 1% unmatched coverage. It includes antialiased
mixtures of the recorded foreground and white; counting only fully opaque color
pixels incorrectly discarded native thin strokes. White-on-white row 16 has no
visible mask and is checked by the exact-color unit test. After an edit, only the
deliberately changed first line is excluded from the geometry comparison.
Package bytes, unrelated parts, undo and editable export/reopen remain checked.

Relevant definitions: MS-DOCX
[CT_SchemeColor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/133bd2fe-ad4c-4422-a120-9c3a1a3a4e30),
[CT_SRgbColor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/10a451b3-6054-4e0a-b1b2-b68fe9316533),
[CT_Percentage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-docx/690e8fcb-f555-4da7-8155-6848901a34df),
and ECMA-376 Part 1 20.1.2.3.20–21. No normative divergence is claimed.
Other color transforms, gradients, opacity and percent-string lexical forms
remain guarded. Standard MCE-view schema checks do not certify W14 semantics.
